title: The Moon Came Back
vol: Mommy Is Human Too · Book Seven
verse: Hard days don't last forever. Keep looking for little glimpses of good, because the light always comes back.

pages.text:
Some mornings wake up heavy, and the sky forgets its blue —
and Mommy's heart was quiet, though she had her work to do.

She drove along the same old street, past sprinklers on a lawn,
and caught — with just one eye — a tiny rainbow. Then… it was gone.

The lady kept on watering. The cars kept rolling by.
But Mommy held that rainbow like a letter from the sky.

"A glimpse," she told the children, "of a promise old and true —
the light that comes after the rain, to say the sun comes through."

"The world drops little presents that most people hurry past —
a bloom inside a sidewalk crack, a shadow on the grass.

They may not mean a single thing to anybody else.
But if they make your heart look up — that glimpse is for yourself."

So Jojo found a feather. Pip, a flower in a crack.
And Baby Bee found Biscuit's tail, which always wags right back.

"But what about the nighttime?" Jojo asked. "When light won't stay?"
"Ah," said Mommy, smiling. "Night has something else to say."

They watched the sky together till the dark had swallowed blue,
and up above the rooftops… the faithful moon came through.

"Every single night," she said, "the moon comes back again.
It doesn't skip the hard nights. It shows up even then.

So when you see it shining, let it whisper what is true:
you're not alone. The light comes back. It always comes for you."

"Some days will feel too heavy. Some nights will feel too long.
But glimpses keep the heart awake until the dark is gone."

Now every day they gather them — a rainbow, bird, or bloom,
and every night they wave hello to the faithful, shining moon.

Because your Mommy's heart gets gray, and she needs glimpses too —
she watches for the rainbow… because she's human too.

items: What is a glimpse you saw today?
What do you do on a heavy day?
Why do you think the moon keeps coming back?
Start a glimpse jar. Write one good thing each day and drop it in.
Look for the moon tonight and wave hello.
